abstract: Research examining how generative AI affects entry barriers to professional occupations and the resulting wage inequality implications. The study finds that while AI raises barriers to entry-level employment (as firms substitute AI for junior workers), the overall wage inequality effects remain modest. AI creates both upward pressure on high-skill wages and reduced demand for entry-level work, but these forces partially offset each other at the aggregate level.
keyFindings: Generative AI raises barriers to entry-level professional employment
Overall wage inequality changes from AI adoption remain modest in magnitude
AI creates upward pressure on high-skill wages while reducing entry-level demand
Offsetting forces at the aggregate level mute the net inequality effect
methodology: Empirical analysis of wage distributions and entry-level hiring patterns at firms adopting generative AI, examining how AI-driven changes in labor demand across skill levels translate into wage inequality measures.
qualifiers: Modest aggregate inequality effects may mask larger distributional shifts within specific occupations or demographics. Early-stage findings that may evolve as AI adoption deepens. Wage inequality measures are sensitive to the specific metric and time horizon used.
